newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Central America eyes coffee quota timetable switch.
newsitem.headline: Central America eyes coffee quota timetable switch.

text.p: Central American coffee producing nations will seek to modify the coffee export quota timetable of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to coincide with the regional crop cycle, Salvadoran coffee officials said Thursday.

In an ACPC meeting scheduled in London next week, Central American nations will propose stretching the existing quota July 1996-June 1997 timetable an extra three months so that it ends in October, Ruben Pineda, the executive director of the Salvadoran Coffee Council told Reuters.
Central America's traditional coffee cycle runs from October to September.
"We would like to negotiate a quarter to end (the quota cycle) with the coffee year of the region," Pineda said.
"It is an administrative proposal, not a substantive one," Herbert de Sola, El Salvador's Presidential Coffee Commissioner also told Reuters.

De Sola explained that, for Central America, the July-June quota cycle is lopsided. In El Salvador, he said, coffee credit cycles are worked out alongside the traditional coffee year and the ACPC quota system is not in tune with that which causes growers financial headaches.

Pineda and De Sola said the ACPC gathering, which will be held alongside the International Coffee Organisation's annual meeting, will also discuss other aspects of coffee exports. Pineda said the export quota system was "going well."
The ACPC is in a second annual cycle of coffee export quotas among member nations in a bid to limit world coffee supply and drive up prices.
